messages:
maria-sales: FYI we kicked off AcmeBank POC today. They want a Private deployment inside their VPC but have a few non-negotiables: preserve client source IP for logging, a single static egress IP for allowlisting, and they run TLS inspection in their DMZ which may affect SNI. They've attached a security questionnaire (see drive link). Can engineering ops propose options?
aj-networking: Quick take: PrivateLink interface endpoints give us private connectivity without peering. But preserving client src IP across PrivateLink -> our infra is tricky unless we keep the customer's ingress path intact (proxy vs NAT).
devon-se: Re: single static egress IP: easiest is a managed egress proxy in the customer VPC that forwards to Redwood via PrivateLink or a dedicated tunnel. That proxy can present a fixed NAT IP. If they need no NAT (literal src IP pass-through) we need routed peering and the customer to accept our ASNs and routing — more friction.
sam-architect: Short pros/cons: 
- PrivateLink: minimal routing changes for customer, better security posture, but client IP preservation requires proxy headers or header pass-through (X-Forwarded-For) — not literal src IP.
- VPC Peering / Transit: literal src IP can be preserved, but customer must handle route acceptance and there are scale/management implications.
- Dedicated connector (reverse proxy hosted in customer VPC): best for allowlist + TLS termination control, adds ~1-2ms latency.
aj-networking: Also call out MTU and TCP MSS issues when doing tunnels/proxies. If their TLS-inspect appliance rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, we need to ensure signature/pinned certs for function-calling still match.
maria-sales: They explicitly asked whether we can support TLS-inspect middlebox (they need it for compliance) or if we require end-to-end TLS. Security wants to know impact on function-calling and model safety.
legalbot: From compliance: E2E TLS to Redwood is preferred. If TLS inspection is performed, customer must document key handling and guarantee HSM separation for any sensitive keys. We cannot accept customer-managed TLS that exposes model prompts or responses to third-party operators unless covered in contract.
devon-se: Implementation checklist snippet for the customer (paste to handoff):
```
# Firewall allowlist (customer outbound to Redwood endpoints)
- 198.51.100.45/32 (redwood-ingress-1) TCP 443
- 198.51.100.46/32 (redwood-ingress-2) TCP 443
- 198.51.101.10/32 (metrics-collector) TCP 443
- NTP: udp 123 to pool.ntp.org or customer NTP server
- DNS: tcp/udp 53 to their resolver
```
Note: if using PrivateLink, replace public IPs with interface endpoint ENIs — allow customer CIDR to those ENIs.
aj-networking: Also add healthcheck endpoints on port 8080 (our side) if they run L4 proxies — share healthcheck CIDR.
maria-sales: Pricing question from customer: if we require a dedicated connector/proxy hosted in their VPC, will that be extra? They want an estimate vs using our hosted PrivateLink endpoints.
sam-architect: Yes — dedicated connector is billed as part of Private deployment setup and may include a monthly infra add-on + egress data charge. I'll loop in pricing to get an estimate. For POC we can offer a time-limited trial of connector without full reserved commit.
devon-se: Ops note: If they need SRC IP in logs for forensics, we can add X-Original-Source-IP headers at the proxy layer and persist them in audit logs. Clarify whether they require network-layer src ip or application layer header is acceptable.
maria-sales: I asked them — they said "network-layer src ip is preferred but app header is acceptable if it's cryptographically signed and tamper-evident." Any thoughts?
aj-networking: We can sign a short HMAC over the header with a shared key between their proxy and our ingress to make header tamper-evident. That solves audit integrity without full peering. Need legal sign-off.
legalbot: HMAC header approach ok with documented key custody and rotation policy. Add to contract: no headers processed as auth unless mutually agreed.
maria-sales: Final POC asks: 1) checklist for customer's netops 2) recommended topology (Privatelink + managed proxy) 3) rough cost delta private-connector vs plain PrivateLink. Who can own the handoff doc?
devon-se: I'll draft the handoff and include the config snippets, healthchecks, and the proxy container template.
aj-networking: I'll produce a diagram and the MTU/TCP MSS notes.
sam-architect: I'll prep the cost delta with pricing ops and mark optional items for POC.
maria-sales: Awesome — can we get initial handoff by EOD tomorrow? Customer wants to start initial connectivity testing next week. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: create POC runbook ticket #POC-842 in eng-oncall.
maria-sales: Thanks all — I'll consolidate replies and send to customer + attached sec questionnaire link.
